In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aflatoxin had no effect on body weight, feed conversion or temperature, and only a minor effect on feed consumption.
the response of the chickens to the aflatoxin was not influenced by the genetic background of the chickens.
the high- and low-line birds were similar in their responses to aflatoxin, and the crosses were similar to their respective parental lines in their responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aflatoxin depressed body growth, feed consumption, feed efficiency, and surface temperatures.
aflatoxin effects are not dependent on antibody response or other traits that are under genetic selection in the populations used.
the effects of dietary aflatoxin on growth, feed conversion, body temperature, and feed consumption in the chicken are similar to those reported for other species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aflatoxin is toxic to chickens at levels as low as 1 microgram/g.
the response to aflatoxin in the chicken is a function of the level of aflatoxin in feed and the age of the birds.
there is no evidence that the immune system plays a major role in the response of birds to dietary aflatoxins.
